root.label: Floating point and numerics
root.note: The standard fixes little; IEEE behaviour is something you test for with is_iec559, not something you get.

children.label: What the standard requires
children.note: Only that float values are a subset of double values, which are a subset of long double; the representation is implementation-defined.

children.label: is_iec559
children.note: numeric_limits<T>::is_iec559 reports IEC 559 (IEEE 754) conformance; static_assert on it to document the dependency.

children.label: Division by zero
children.note: Formally undefined in [expr.mul]; IEEE platforms give an infinity or NaN.

children.label: Extended types (C++23)
children.note: <stdfloat> adds optional float16_t to float128_t and bfloat16_t, each a distinct type from float, double and long double.

children.label: Equality and ordering
children.note: Floating-point comparison is not a total order, and equality is the wrong tool for computed values.
Each literal and the sum are rounded to the binary grid, so the sum lands one step from the nearest double to 0.3.

children.label: NaN compares
children.note: A NaN is unequal to everything including itself, and only != is true.

children.label: partial_ordering
children.note: <=> on floating point returns partial_ordering, whose unordered value fails less, equal and greater tests.

children.label: Signed zero
children.note: +0.0 equals -0.0, but signbit, copysign and a bit_cast can tell them apart.

children.label: Precision and rounding
children.note: Results can differ between builds because the standard permits wider evaluation and fused operations.

children.label: Excess precision
children.note: [expr.pre] lets operands and results use more range and precision than their type, without changing the type.

children.label: FLT_EVAL_METHOD
children.note: The <cfloat> macro that reports the evaluation format; 0 means each operation uses its own type.

children.label: Contraction and fma
children.note: A fused a*b+c rounds once; std::fma asks for that, and -ffp-contract=off forbids it.

children.label: Conversions
children.note: Narrowing from floating point can be undefined, and constant evaluation exposes it.

children.label: Float to int
children.note: Truncates toward zero; undefined when the result does not fit, including for infinities and NaNs.

children.label: Float to float
children.note: In range but inexact picks a neighbour, implementation-defined; out of range is undefined.

children.label: Constant evaluation
children.note: An out-of-range float-to-int conversion is not a constant expression, so constexpr rejects it.

children.label: Library helpers
children.note: Utilities that avoid the usual overflow, endpoint and text-conversion mistakes.

children.label: midpoint
children.note: Overflow-free average; integer results round toward the first argument.

children.label: lerp
children.note: Exact at t == 0 and t == 1, monotonic in t, and extrapolates outside the unit interval.

children.label: to_chars and from_chars
children.note: Shortest text that parses back exactly, guaranteed only within one implementation.

children.label: numbers constants
children.note: pi, e and friends as double variables, with _v variable templates for other types.

children.label: Constexpr math and fast-math
children.note: Which cmath functions work at compile time, and why optimization flags can leave the standard.

children.label: C++23 constexpr cmath
children.note: Functions independent of the floating-point environment, such as fabs, floor and fma, became constexpr.

children.label: C++26 constexpr cmath
children.note: Most remaining functions, including sqrt and sin, became constexpr in C++26.

children.label: -ffast-math
children.note: Licenses reassociation and ignoring NaN, infinity and signed zero; the program no longer follows the standard's rules.
